entity.name_th: อโศก / สุขุมวิท
entity.scope_notes: 800 m straight-line catchment around the BTS Asok / MRT Sukhumvit interchange; both physical stops share the single scored area st.asok. District split (app data): Watthana 51.3%, Khlong Toei 48.7% — it is not all of either district. Research-verified locations: Terminal 21 (~147 m) and Soi Cowboy (~121 m) inside; Benjakitti Park northeast tip ~460 m inside but main entrances and most of its area beyond 800 m; Benchasiri Park (~958 m) outside; Bumrungrad Hospital (~1.2 km) outside.

question_answers.notes: Unit = the 800 m straight-line catchment around the BTS Asok / MRT Sukhumvit interchange (Thai: อโศก / สุขุมวิท; road: Asok Montri Rd = Soi Sukhumvit 21). The station itself spans Watthana and Khlong Toei districts (matches app split 51.3/48.7). Verified inside: interchange, Terminal 21 (~150 m), Soi Cowboy (~120 m), mouths of Sois 11/15/19/23, Exchange Tower (~230 m), Benjakitti Park's north tip (~460-510 m). Verified outside: Benchasiri Park (~960 m), Bumrungrad International (~1.2 km), most of Benjakitti's area (far side 1.3-1.5 km). Partial: the long sois, Asok Montri footpath corridor, and the Sukhumvit corridor characterization. Srinakharinwirot University is listed by Wikipedia among station landmarks but its representative point is ~990 m — likely outside or edge-inside, unverified.

Everyday experience differs sharply by block and hour: weekday office-worker flows through the interchange (offices at the corner, hotels and skyscrapers corridor), tourists funneled to Soi Cowboy after dark, soi-level dining (Korean Soi 12, Middle Eastern, Terminal 21 food court). Sources are guide voices; a resident-sourced account (Reddit) was not fetchable this session.

The single most cited benefit is the two-line interchange: one change point reaching Siam, Silom/Sathorn, Chatuchak and the airport link, which reduces car dependence — a mechanism (network position), not just an adjective. Secondary: dense everyday essentials (61 convenience stores, 8 supermarkets within 800 m). Keep distinct: 'most connected in the city' is guide framing; the two-line crossing is verified fact.

Counter-evidence deliberately gathered: platform crowding (2016 editorial 'horrific'; 2026-09-25 evening-rush failure packed Asok platform-to-gate), crumbling 30-year-old footpaths with mud-splash tiles now being renovated, noise from two roads + two rails + Cowboy strip, no major hospital inside 800 m, and premium asking rents. No source found on scams around the nightlife strip this session (TripAdvisor/forum pages returned 403).

Rhythm: weekday office peaks swell the interchange (evening-rush failure shows saturation); nightlife strips define late evening; parks run dawn to 21:00/22:00. Pockets rather than one mood: Cowboy block and main-road frontage vs deeper side sois; guides advise testing the 07:30-09:30 window before renting. Seasonal claims (rain slowing works) come only from a search snippet, not a body-read — not claimed.

Transfer is at one point: BTS Asok to MRT Sukhumvit via Exit 3 / connecting walkway. Walking surface is the weak link: BMA's own announcement describes 30+-year-old tiles on sand that collapse and splash mud along Asok Montri. Sidewalk shade, crossing detail and canal/expressway barriers were not separately evidenced this session. Condo-to-MRT direct links exist for some buildings (guide claim).

Groceries: 8 supermarket-type entries incl. Tops, Foodland, Villa Market, MaxValu, Makro Food Service (Sukhumvit 22) within 800 m; 2 marketplaces incl. SW1; 61 convenience stores. Healthcare: pharmacies/small clinics inside; nearest full hospital ~1.2 km. Work/study: Exchange Tower and office towers at the corner; SWU campus likely just outside (unverified edge). Terminal 21 covers mall retail.

Affordability = a real premium but not uniformly luxury: portal asking rents 30-48k (1-bed) and 38-130k+ (2-bed) in Nov 2026 listings, guide ranges 20-40k / 35-60k, app DooAsset medians 26.5k/55k (n=30/18, station-override proxy, 2026-10-25). All figures are asking prices; no signed-rent data found; portal 'near E4' radius undefined; page-1 sample skews premium. The rent=4 (expensive) score is consistent with the range of evidence.

Location check resolves the lead: Benjakitti's NE tip is inside the 800 m radius (~460 m), but the park's main Ratchadaphisek/QSNCC-side entrances and most of its 72 ha lie beyond it — web sources circulate both '500 m' and '1.1 km' figures, both partly right (edge vs entrance). Benchasiri Park is outside (~960 m). Hours 04:30-21:00/22:00 (conflicting). Tree-lined-street greenery quality: not evidenced.

Conditional fit: commuters and car-free workers gain most (two lines, one interchange); quiet-seekers and home-all-day remote workers fit worst; families are pointed one stop out; nightlife workers/tourists trade convenience for noise. Avoid demographic stereotypes: the guides' own audience framing (office workers, students, expats) is used rather than assumptions.

Change: BMA footpath renovation along Asok Montri announced 2025-03-18, contractor targeted by July 2025 — completion unverified (recheck). Dated event (not a change): BTS failure 2026-09-25 evening rush with Asok platform-to-gate overflow. Forest-park expansion completed 2022 (older context). No verified 2024-2026 openings/closures of venues inside the unit were found this session; a search-snippet mention of rain slowing works was not body-verified.

Score cross-check without editing: crowd=1 strongly corroborated (multiple sources, incl. a 2026 event); daily_essentials=10 corroborated by OSM counts; food/nightlife=10 corroborated qualitatively; rent=4 consistent with asking-rent ranges; green=9 hinges on Benjakitti's edge being inside while most of the park is not — a defensible but fragile basis; transport=8 sits below guide enthusiasm ('most connected') — calibration question, not an error; safety=6 and gym_sports=10 have no supporting source evidence found this session (no crime data, no gym audit) and remain outside the qualitative record. Uncertainty: no recent station-level ridership split.

preview.text_en: Two rail lines, Terminal 21 and Soi Cowboy all meet at one corner — and the closest edge of Benjakitti Park is about 460 m away, with its main entrances beyond the 800 m catchment.

guide_lead.text_en: Asok is Bangkok's crossroads more than its neighborhood: the only place where the BTS Sukhumvit Line and the MRT Blue Line meet, with Terminal 21 at the corner, Exchange Tower offices on one side and the Soi Cowboy bar strip about a block away. Guides rate it the easiest place in Bangkok to live without a car, and the 800 m catchment is dense with convenience stores, supermarkets and cheap soi food. The price of that position is paid daily — one of the city's most crowded station platforms, noise from two roads, two rail lines and the bar soi, and footpaths old enough that the city government announced their rebuild in 2025. It fits people who will use the interchange every day; it wears down people who will hear it from home.

strengths.text_en: The two-line interchange means most of central Bangkok is reachable without a car, and guides describe residents here giving up taxis almost entirely.
Everyday essentials are unusually dense within 800 m: 61 convenience stores, eight supermarket-type stores (Tops, Foodland, Villa Market, Makro Food Service among them) and two marketplaces.
Eating out runs from a Korean community cluster on Soi 12 to Middle Eastern and Thai soi kitchens and Terminal 21's food court, so daily food does not require traveling.
The northern tip of Benjakitti Park crosses into the catchment, putting a running-loop edge within a few hundred meters even though the main entrances sit farther out.

tradeoffs.text_en: Crowding is structural, not occasional: a 2016 editorial ranked Asok's crowds 1/5, and when one BTS train failed at the evening rush in September 2026, passengers backed up from Asok's platform to the street-level gates.
Noise stacks up from three directions — Sukhumvit and Asok Montri roads, the two rail viaducts, and the Soi Cowboy strip — which is why guides tell renters to go five minutes deep into a side soi.
The walk to the stations ran for decades on 30-year-old paving tiles that collapse and splash mud; the BMA promised a rebuild starting 2025 but completion is not yet verified.
Rents carry a location premium and the nearest full hospital (Bumrungrad) is about 1.2 km out — everyday medicine here means pharmacies and small clinics.

day_night.text_en: Weekday mornings and early evenings belong to office commuters squeezing through the interchange, while late evening shifts the center of gravity to the ~40 bars of Soi Cowboy and the tourist flow around Terminal 21 — the same corner, two different crowds.
Green time is bounded by park hours (04:30 to about 21:00-22:00), so the quietest window in the unit is early morning before the office rush fills Asok Montri.

within_area_variation.text_en: The difference between blocks is bigger than the difference between hours: Cowboy's bar row sits ~120 m from the interchange while the mouths of Sois 15, 19 and 23 carry office and apartment life, and Soi 11 mixes guesthouses with residences a few hundred meters west.

South of Sukhumvit, the catchment crosses into Khlong Toei district and reaches the edge of Benjakitti's lake-and-forest section; park-facing addresses there are explicitly marketed at a premium over sois without a view.

Guides characterize the area as having less identity than Thonglor or Silom — it is picked for the crossroads, which is why side-soi selection (window orientation, distance from the main road) does most of the work in whether a given unit is livable.

conditional_fit.text_en: Strong fit: commuters who change lines daily, airport travelers via Makkasan, and workers in the surrounding towers who want a car-free routine.
Poor fit: quiet-seekers and home-all-day remote workers, per the guides' own verdicts; families wanting calm are pointed one stop east to Phrom Phong.

Situational fit: nightlife workers and frequent visitors trade the Cowboy strip's convenience against its noise; anyone prioritizing park life should treat Benjakitti as a park whose nearest edge is about 460 m away and whose main entrances lie beyond the catchment, not a doorstep one.

uncertainties: No recent (2024-2026) station-level ridership breakdown for BTS Asok vs MRT Sukhumvit vs transfer flows was found; crowding rests on editorial and event evidence.
All rent figures are asking prices; signed-contract levels and the portal's 'near E4' radius are unknown, and the app's DooAsset medians rest on n=30/18.
Whether the 2025 Asok Montri footpath renovation was completed, and to what standard, is unverified.
Benjakitti Park opening hours conflict (04:30-21:00 per Wikipedia vs 04:30-22:00 per OSM), and entrance positions are not individually mapped.
Safety (app score 6) and gym/sports provision (app score 10) found no supporting qualitative or quantitative sources this session.
Whether the app's '15.3 ha park within 800 m' corresponds to Benjakitti's portion inside the radius is an unverified inference.
Resident-voiced accounts (Reddit r/Bangkok threads, TripAdvisor and ExpatForum discussions) were all blocked or paywalled this session.
